skill.name: hypothesis-generation
skill.description: Structured hypothesis formulation from observations. Use when you have experimental observations or data and need to formulate testable hypotheses with predictions, propose mechanisms, and design experiments to test them. Follows scientific method framework. For open-ended ideation use scientific-brainstorming; for automated LLM-driven hypothesis testing on datasets use hypogenic.
skill.summary: Generate evidence-based, testable scientific hypotheses with predictions and experiment plans.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

content.value_statement: Researchers need to turn observations into clear, testable explanations. This skill structures evidence review, competing hypotheses, predictions, and experiment plans.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies observations, scope, constraints, and scientific domains before hypothesis generation.
Guides literature search across PubMed, web sources, reviews, and primary studies.
Produces competing mechanistic hypotheses with assumptions, evidence, and weaknesses.
Evaluates hypotheses for testability, falsifiability, parsimony, and explanatory power.
Designs experiments with controls, measurements, confounds, and falsifying outcomes.
Formats results as a structured LaTeX hypothesis report with appendices.
limitations: Requires accurate source material and domain context from the user.
Does not replace expert review, ethics approval, or statistical consultation.
May need web access to collect recent literature and citations.
Generated hypotheses remain provisional until tested with evidence.

use_cases.title: Plan a Thesis Project
use_cases.description: Convert preliminary observations into competing hypotheses, measurable predictions, and experiments for a research proposal.

use_cases.title: Explore Product Research Signals
use_cases.description: Analyze unexpected experimental results and produce mechanistic explanations with tests for the next lab cycle.

use_cases.title: Review Research Directions
use_cases.description: Compare several scientific explanations and prioritize the studies most likely to distinguish them.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Initial Hypotheses
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single observation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this observation: [observation]. Generate three testable hypotheses, key assumptions, and one prediction for each.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Explanations
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these observations: [observations]. Create competing hypotheses, rank them by testability, and list evidence needed to distinguish them.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Experiments
prompt_templates.prompt: For this hypothesis: [hypothesis]. Propose experiments, controls, measurements, confounds, and falsifying outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a complete structured deliverable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a structured hypothesis report for [phenomenon]. Include literature search strategy, competing mechanisms, predictions, experimental designs, and appendix-ready evidence notes.

output_examples.input: Observation: Cell growth slows after treatment, but viability remains high.
output: Three competing mechanisms that explain slowed growth without cell death.
Predictions for cell-cycle markers, metabolic activity, and recovery after washout.
Two experiments with controls that separate cytostasis from delayed toxicity.

output_examples.input: Observation: A biomarker rises before symptoms in a longitudinal cohort.
output: Causal, compensatory, and confounded association hypotheses.
Quality assessment across testability, parsimony, and explanatory power.
A study plan using time-lag analysis, matched controls, and validation cohorts.

output_examples.input: Goal: Prepare a hypothesis report for a grant planning meeting.
output: Executive summary with prioritized hypotheses and key evidence.
Prediction matrix showing results that support or falsify each explanation.
Appendix outline for literature, protocols, assumptions, and limitations.

best_practices: Provide the core observation, domain, existing data, and known constraints before starting.
Ask for competing hypotheses rather than a single preferred explanation.
Review proposed experiments with domain experts before using them in real studies.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to confirm a preferred hypothesis without testing alternatives.
Treating generated citations or mechanisms as verified without source review.
Skipping controls, confounds, and falsifying outcomes in experiment plans.

faq.question: What does this skill help produce?
faq.answer: It helps produce testable scientific hypotheses, predictions, experiment plans, and structured hypothesis reports.

faq.question: Can it search the latest literature?
faq.answer: It can guide literature search and use available web tools when the environment provides them.

faq.question: Does it replace a subject matter expert?
faq.answer: No. Expert review is still needed for feasibility, safety, ethics, and interpretation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Provide observations, measurements, study context, constraints, and relevant papers or datasets.

faq.question: Can it create publication-ready reports?
faq.answer: It can draft a structured LaTeX report, but final content and citations need review.
